claims.text: Yttrium-doped powder-pack boronizing will form a continuous, ultrathin Y-rich borate/oxide surface scale on TiB2-based components.
The Y-rich surface scale will reduce corrosion by molten aluminum.
A treatment temperature of 850–900 °C is suitable for the proposed Y-doped boronizing treatment.
An inert or mildly reducing treatment atmosphere will promote formation of the proposed scale.
Controlled cooling will promote scale uniformity and strong adhesion.
The treatment will form a Y-rich oxide/borate layer along grain boundaries as well as at the surface.
During boronizing, yttrium segregates to the surface.
Surface-segregated yttrium reacts at high temperature to form a stable Y-rich borate/oxide layer.
The resulting Y-rich layer is adherent to the TiB2-based substrate.
The Y-rich layer acts as a diffusion barrier against aluminum.
The diffusion barrier hinders aluminum penetration into the substrate.
The diffusion barrier hinders reaction between molten aluminum and the substrate.
The Y-doped treatment will decrease molten-aluminum penetration depth relative to untreated TiB2 components.
The Y-doped treatment will decrease the attacked surface area relative to untreated TiB2 components.
Decreased penetration and attacked area will reduce the corrosion rate.
The treatment will remain effective under conditions typical of hot-dip aluminum plating.
Temperatures significantly above 900 °C may limit the durability and performance of the Y-rich scale.
Highly oxidizing atmospheres may limit the durability and performance of the Y-rich scale.
Variation in scale uniformity may cause variation in the magnitude of corrosion improvement.
Minor scale inhomogeneities may cause localized failure during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is framed against untreated TiB2, the baseline permits either undoped boronizing or no boronizing, and the falsification experiment uses undoped boronizing. These non-equivalent comparators make the claimed relative improvement ambiguous.
